So the page structure is:
- Page 1: Title, abstract
- Pages 2-4: Method sections
- Pages 5-6: Experiments (tables)
- Page 7: More experiments
- Page 8: Section 7 (Discussion and Conclusion) starts
- Page 9: Limitations section starts
- Page 10+: References and Appendix

So main body = pages 1-8, with Section 7 (Discussion and Conclusion) on page 8, then Limitations on page 9. That's exactly 8 pages of main content. References start somewhere around pages 10-12, and appendix from page 13 onward.


The `\clearpage` before Limitations forces it onto page 9, so the core sections occupy pages 1-8 within the limit, with Limitations, references, and appendix following separately. Now I'm organizing my findings to compile a complete review, starting with a summary of OntoCoDec and its approach to compiling IE ontology schemas into composable decoding constraints.

For novelty, the key contributions are the stateful entity registry that maintains type information during generation and the sequential masking strategy that conditions tail types on head types. This extends grammar-constrained decoding into semantic territory, which is a clear step beyond existing work like XGrammar and Outlines, though it shares token-level filtering similarities with approaches like PICARD.

The closest precedent is GCD's application of grammar constraints to IE, but OntoCoDec layers semantic constraints on top through its dynamic registry. Training-based methods like GoLLIE offer complementary soft guidance rather than hard constraints, while EnriCo and IterGen require more manual overhead. Overall, it's a solid engineering contribution that's practically useful—extending proven paradigms rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts.

Now looking at the writing quality, the narrative flows reasonably well from problem to method to experiments, and the motivation is concrete. But I'm noticing some structural issues: the abstract is bloated with 201 words and too many experimental results crammed in, the contribution list is dense and hard to parse, and the conclusion feels rushed. These are presentation problems that could be tightened up.

The Related Work section is particularly compressed—just one paragraph in the main text that reads more like a citation dump, though there's a more comprehensive treatment in the appendix. The abstract itself introduces too many abbreviations upfront and reads more like a technical specification than a compelling overview of the work.

Looking at the appendix coverage, the paper does a solid job positioning itself across five different paradigms: grammar-constrained decoding approaches, code-domain semantic constraints, vocabulary-constrained information extraction, training-based methods, and post-hoc validation techniques. But there are some notable gaps—InstructUIE, UniversalNER, and a few other recent works aren't mentioned.

The bibliography has 55 unique citations, which is reasonable for EMNLP, though there are 8 orphan entries that look like duplicate variants of the same papers (different naming conventions for the same work). The format checks out: it's using the review package for anonymous submission, stays within the 8-page limit, and follows ACL guidelines properly.

The abstract is within the word count range, and both the limitations and ethics sections are present. However, the Responsible NLP Research Checklist is missing entirely—that's a required component for EMNLP 2026. There's also a duplicate bibliography key that needs cleaning up.

The main substantive issue is that the paper's core claim about "near-lossless composability" doesn't align with the actual results showing cross-field consistency violations up to 12.02% in some cases. The abstract and contribution framing oversell this without adequately qualifying the limitation.

The WikiEvents evaluation is another concern—with only 20 documents in the test set, the results are too preliminary to feature so prominently in the abstract and main contributions. The confidence intervals would be quite wide, which undermines the generalization claims.

The related work section is also underdeveloped in the main text, compressed into a single dense paragraph when a top-venue paper needs more substantial coverage there. The detailed survey in the appendix doesn't compensate since reviewers focus on the main body.

The abstract itself is packed with too many numbers and reads more like a results table than a coherent narrative—the four core research questions get lost in the density of metrics.

Contribution 3 is trying to do too much in one bullet point: composability with LoRA, the CF↔DR trade-off analysis, zero-shot robustness across multiple models, and beam search results all bundled together. This needs to be split into separate contributions or substantially streamlined.

The DocRED grammar-only result where DR actually increases (26.17% from 18.46%) is counterintuitive and deserves clearer explanation in the main text so reviewers don't get confused by this phenomenon.

There's also a disconnect between the narrative about constraint tightness correlating with DR and what the data actually shows—the dual-factor linear model only has 4 data points with p≈0.058 (not statistically significant) and excludes Mistral, so presenting this as a finding is overstated.

Beyond that, there are 8 orphan bibliography entries with duplicates, the conclusion is just one paragraph when it should be more substantial, and I should double-check the Responsible NLP Research Checklist before finalizing the review.

## 总体评分
**Overall**: 3.0 (Findings)
**一句话总结**: 技术执行扎实、实验覆盖充分，但核心新颖性为已有范式的工程组合，CF trade-off 未解决，限制了实际贡献深度。

## 官方维度打分（来自 ACL ARR Review Form）

| 维度 | 分数 | 理由摘要 |
|------|------|----------|
| Soundness | 3.5/5 | 双层约束设计在技术上合理，ablation 充分；但 CF trade-off 在 zero-shot 下将总违规率仅从 15.45% 降至 10.83%（SciERC），"near-lossless" 的 claim 需要更多限定 |
| Excitement | 2.5/5 | 将 grammar-constrained decoding 从语法扩展到语义对 IE 社区有实用价值，但核心技术是 XGrammar + stateful logit processor 的工程组合，缺乏范式级突破 |
| Reproducibility | 4/5 | 详细的超参数、硬件配置、seed，承诺开源；但代码当前不可获取 |
| Reviewer Confidence | 4/5 | 熟悉 constrained decoding 和 LLM-based IE 领域 |

## Must-Fix 问题（影响接收决定）

**N1** [critical] CF trade-off 与 "near-lossless composability" claim 不一致
- 具体位置：Abstract L6, §1 Contribution 3, §7 结论第一句
- 问题：Abstract 声称 "near-lossless composability" 并在 Contribution 3 中列出 "DR≤0.20% at <0.6pp F1 cost"，但这仅报告了 DR 下降，忽略了 CF 从 0→9.90%（SciERC zero-shot）甚至 12.02%（Llama DocRED）的增长。在 SciERC 上，total type-violation burden（DR+CF）从 15.45% 降至 10.83%，即总违规仅减少了约 30%，而非 Abstract 暗示的 94%。Fine-tuning 将 CF 压至≤1.18%，但 "near-lossless" 在 zero-shot 场景下不成立。
- 为什么影响接收：核心 claim 的准确性直接影响审稿人对贡献的信任度。过度宣传是 ARR 常见拒稿理由。
- 建议修改方向：(1) Abstract 和 Contribution 中明确区分 zero-shot 与 fine-tuned 场景的 DR+CF 总量；(2) "near-lossless" 仅限定于 fine-tuned 场景；(3) 在 Abstract 中提及 CF trade-off 而非将其隐藏在正文中。

**N2** [critical] WikiEvents 评估过于初步，但在 Abstract 和 Contributions 中占较大权重
- 具体位置：Abstract L10-11, §1 Contribution 3 ("EE: RoV→0%, AC≤0.8%"), §5.5
- 问题：WikiEvents 仅在 20 个测试文档上进行 fine-tuning composability 评估。论文自称 "preliminary"（§5.5 L64），但 Abstract 和 Contribution 列表中将 EE 结果与 RE 结果并列呈现，未做显著标注。20 个文档的 confidence interval 极宽（论文自述 "wide confidence intervals at this sample size"），trigger F1 出现 -5.4pp 的波动。
- 为什么影响接收：将初步结果包装为与主要结果同等级别的 contribution，是 claim 膨胀的表现。
- 建议修改方向：(1) Abstract 中明确标注 EE 结果为 "preliminary"；(2) 降低 EE 在 Contribution list 中的权重或单独列为 "preliminary" contribution；(3) 增加更大规模 EE 数据集验证（如 ACE2005）。

**N3** [critical] 缺少 Responsible NLP Research Checklist
- 具体位置：main.tex 全文搜索 "checklist" / "Responsible" 均无结果
- 问题：ARR 2026 要求提交 Responsible NLP Research Checklist，缺失可能导致 desk reject。
- 建议：按照 ARR 官方模板补充 checklist，逐项认真填写。

## Should-Fix 问题（影响评分但不一票否决）

- 问题：整个 Related Work 只有一个段落，将 30+ 篇引用压缩成连续的 citation cluster（如 `\cite{..., ..., ..., ..., ..., ..., ...}`）。虽然 Appendix A 有详细的 extended survey（111 行），但审稿人主要评估正文质量。当前正文的 Related Work 更像 citation list 而非有结构的 positioning。
- 建议：扩展为 2-3 个 paragraph，分别覆盖 grammar-constrained decoding、schema-aware IE training、post-hoc validation 三个主要范式，每段最后一句说明 OntoCoDec 的差异。可将 §7 的部分讨论内容合并以节省空间。

**W2** [warning] Abstract 数据密度过高，叙事被数字淹没
- 具体位置：abstract.tex
- 问题：201 词的 Abstract 中包含约 15 个数字/百分比、7 个缩写（IE, LLM, DR, LoRA, CF, RE, EE），密度过高。审稿人无法在 30 秒内抓住核心价值。"Beam search ($k{=}4$) with LoRA eliminates all four violation types on SciERC" 这类细节不应出现在 Abstract 中。
- 建议：减少到 2-3 个关键数字，将 beam search 和 WikiEvents 细节移至正文。

**W3** [warning] Contribution 3 信息过载
- 具体位置：§1 Introduction, enumerate item 3 (section1_introduction_draft.tex L30)
- 问题：单条 contribution 包含至少 5 个独立 claim：composability with LoRA、CF↔DR trade-off analysis、zero-shot robustness across 4 models、WikiEvents EE、beam search。每个 claim 都附带具体数字。审稿人难以判断哪些是核心贡献。
- 建议：拆分为 2-3 条，或精简为一条带有明确主语的 claim（如 "Empirical validation of composability..."），将细节留给正文。

**W4** [warning] Dual-factor pattern 统计支撑不足
- 具体位置：§4 L29, Appendix B (appendix_discussion.tex L93)
- 问题：Constraint tightness × baseline violation rate 的 dual-factor 模型仅基于 n=4 个 data points（排除 Mistral 后），p≈0.058（>0.05），R²=0.886 但 df=2。论文承认 "descriptive characterization rather than a confirmatory statistical test"，但主文中的表述 "This dual-factor pattern... is consistent with the cross-dataset results" 可能让读者误以为这是 confirmed finding。
- 建议：在主文中明确标注这是 descriptive observation（n=4），降低 claim 强度。

**W5** [warning] DocRED grammar-only DR 增加的解释不充分
- 具体位置：§5.3 Table 3, §5.3 "Layer contributions" paragraph (section5_docred_draft.tex L67)
- 问题：Grammar-only 将 DocRED 的 DR 从 18.46% 增加到 26.17%（+42%）。这是一个反直觉的结果：约束反而增加了违规。论文在一句话中解释为 "OOV triples become evaluable and expose latent type incompatibilities"，但这值得更详细的讨论，因为它直接影响对 grammar layer 贡献的理解。
- 建议：增加 2-3 句话解释 OOV→evaluable 的 pipeline 逻辑，可能需要一个小例子。

**W6** [warning] §7 Discussion and Conclusion 过于简短
- 具体位置：section7_conclusion_compressed.tex（仅 6 行正文，1 个段落）
- 问题：对于一篇 8 页的论文，Discussion and Conclusion 只有 1 个段落（约 100 词），而 Limitations 有 3 个段落。Conclusion 没有讨论 broader impact、future work 方向（除了 CF 的一句话）、或 contribution 的归纳。
- 建议：扩展到至少 2 段，增加 future work 讨论（如 global entity consensus 如何实现、更多 IE 任务的扩展）。

- **Bib 重复条目**：`schall2025hiddencost` 出现两次；`boostcd2025`/`sakota2025boostcd`、`guidex2025`/`delafuente2025guidex`、`slot2025`/`shen2025slot` 等多对重复（内容相同但 key 不同）。共 8 个 orphan bib entries，应清理。
- **Reference 验证**：`regino2025kgcurator` 在 OpenAlex 中未找到完全匹配，`vukovic2024dore` 无结果，`formattax2026` 无结果（可能太新）。建议核实这三篇引用的真实性和完整信息。
- **Footnote 1**（section3_method_draft.tex L34）：33.3% 和 36.8% spurious pairs 的计算有信息量但脚注位置打断了正文流；可考虑移至 appendix。
- **Table caption 自包含性**：Table 1 caption 中 "Grammar-only represents the ceiling of grammar-constrained decoding~\cite{geng2023gcd}" 做了不必要的 claim，caption 应仅描述表格内容。
- **`\clearpage` before Limitations**：导致 page 8 底部有空白。如果主体内容已经紧凑到 8 页，可以不用 `\clearpage`，让 Limitations 自然接续。

## Questions（需要作者回答）

**Q1**: CF↔DR trade-off 的 Pareto 前沿是否意味着在 per-slot enforcement 框架内，无论如何调参都无法同时降低 DR 和 CF？如果是，是否有理论论证或更多的 ablation 数据点来支持这一结论？

**Q2**: Table 2 中 Qwen LoRA 的 DR=0% vs Llama LoRA 的 DR=0.09%——这个差异是统计显著的吗？还是在 confidence interval 内？如果 Llama 的 CI 覆盖了 0%，那么 "DR≤0.20%" 的 claim 可以进一步加强。

**Q3**: Constraint tightness κ 是从 training data 的 observed type pairs 中提取的（§5 setup），而非从 formal ontology。如果 training data 的覆盖不完全（即某些合法的 type pair 在训练集中未出现），constraint table 会比真实 ontology 更紧。这种 coverage gap 对 DR 和 F1 的影响有多大？

**Q4**: 为什么 Mistral 被排除在 dual-factor 分析之外但仍保留在 cross-model validation 中？如果 Mistral 属于不同 regime（calibration 不足），是否应该更清楚地框定 OntoCoDec 的适用范围？

**Q5**: Beam search + LoRA 在 SciERC 上消除了所有四种 violation——这个结果在 DocRED 上是否也成立？如果不成立，原因是什么？

---

## Missing References

1. **InstructUIE** (Wang et al., 2023, "InstructUIE: Multi-task Instruction Tuning for Unified Information Extraction") - 直接相关的 instruction-tuned IE 方法，缺失。
2. **UniversalNER** (Zhou et al., 2024) - 用 LLM 做 universal NER，schema-aware 训练的重要参考。
3. **Wadhwa et al. (2023), "Revisiting Relation Extraction in the era of Large Language Models"** - LLM-based RE 的系统评估，直接相关。
4. **DeepStruct** (Wang et al., 2022) - 结构化预测训练方法。
5. **BioREx** (Luo et al., 2022) - 生物医学 RE 中的 constraint-based 方法，与 RELATE 互补。

---

## 主要优势

- **S1**: 问题定义清晰有价值——DR violations 在 LLM-based IE 中确实普遍存在，且论文用具体数字量化了问题规模（15-18% baseline DR）。
- **S2**: 实验覆盖面广——3 个模型 × 3 个数据集 × 2 个 regime（zero-shot + fine-tuned），加上 ablation（5-way on SciERC, 4-way on DocRED）、beam search、runtime、scalability，形成了完整的 evaluation matrix。
- **S3**: CF trade-off 的诚实讨论——论文没有回避 CF 增加的问题，提供了 fallback ablation（Table 7）、CF distribution 分析（Table 8）、和 Pareto 前沿讨论，这是负责任的学术实践。
- **S4**: 跨 tokenizer 的通用设计——continuation masking 处理了 byte-level BPE 和 SentencePiece 的差异，三个不同 tokenizer family 验证了方法的通用性。
- **S5**: Composability 是一个有价值的设计目标——证明 constrained decoding 可以与 fine-tuning 无缝组合（DR≤0.20%, R-F1 ±0.6pp），这对部署有实际意义。

---

## Detailed Comments（逐节）

**§1 Introduction**: 叙事线整体清晰（DR violations 存在 → 现有方法不足 → OntoCoDec 方案）。但第一段从 "LLMs are increasingly used for IE" 开头略泛，可以更具体地从一个 motivating example 切入。Contribution 3 严重过载（见 W3）。

**§2 Background**: 简洁清晰。Constraint tightness 的定义（Eq. ∅）在这里首次出现，但在 §4 又重复定义（Eq. 2），应统一。

**§3 Method**: 技术描述清晰。Sequential masking（head type → conditional range）的设计是方法的核心创新点，non-rectangularity 的分析（33-37% spurious pairs）提供了有力的 motivation。Grammar-semantic interaction 的 enabling dependency 解释得当。

**§4 Constraint Composition**: 形式化处理得当。Grammar-first fallback 的设计合理（structural > semantic priority）。但建议将 constraint tightness 定义统一到 §2，此处不重复。

**§5 Experiments**: 
- SciERC ablation（Table 1）结构清晰，五向对比有说服力。
- DocRED 结果中 grammar-only DR 增加需要更多解释（见 W5）。
- Cross-model validation 覆盖充分，但 Mistral 的 boundary condition 讨论可以更系统化。
- WikiEvents 结果有价值但 preliminary caveat 应更突出。
- Runtime overhead 报告简洁但完整。
- Beam search 结果令人印象深刻（消除所有 violation types），但仅限 SciERC。

**§6 Related Work**: 主体段落过于压缩（见 W1）。Appendix A 的 extended survey 质量高，分类体系合理（5 个 paradigm），positioning 清晰。但审稿人不应被迫翻附录来理解 positioning。

**§7 Conclusion**: 过于简短（见 W6）。缺乏 future work 讨论和 broader impact 思考。

**Limitations**: 内容充实且诚实。三个段落分别覆盖 constraint scope、evaluation coverage、engineering considerations。CF trade-off 讨论详尽。但部分内容（如 "residual DR decomposition"）过于细节化，可以精简。

**Ethics Statement**: 简洁但足够。

**Appendix**: 内容丰富（extended related work, discussion, per-relation analysis, sampling, beam search, reproducibility, doc length, prompt sensitivity, case studies, scalability, full fine-tuning），约 18 页。整体质量高，支撑了主文的 claims。

**格式检查**:
- ✅ `\usepackage[review]{acl}` 正确
- ✅ 匿名化完整（"Anonymous ACL submission"）
- ✅ 主体 8 页
- ✅ Limitations 独立 section，不计页数
- ✅ Ethics Statement 存在
- ❌ **Responsible NLP Research Checklist 缺失**
- ✅ Abstract ~201 词
- ✅ 无 em-dash 滥用（仅在注释中）
- ✅ 无 en-dash 解释性用法
- ⚠️ Bib 有 8 个 orphan entries 和 1 个 duplicate key

---

**Overall Assessment**: 3.0 / 5 (Findings) | **Confidence**: 4 / 5

**理由**: 论文针对 LLM-based IE 的 type violation 问题提出了一个技术上合理的两层约束解码方案。实验覆盖面广、ablation 充分、CF trade-off 讨论诚实。主要不足在于：(1) 核心新颖性是现有技术（XGrammar + stateful logit masking）的工程组合而非新范式；(2) CF trade-off 在 zero-shot 下将总违规率仅降低约 30%，与 "near-lossless" 的宣传不符；(3) WikiEvents EE 评估过于初步（20 文档）；(4) Related Work 主文过度压缩。论文适合 Findings track：执行质量高、结果有实用价值，但 novelty 和 contribution 深度不足以达到 Conference 水平。

现在将审稿意见汇报给 Review Director。

The paper does acknowledge this in §5 setup ("RE type constraints are extracted automatically from observed type pairs in training data; neither dataset provides a formal ontology") and in Limitations ("Schema coverage gaps arise because RE constraints are extracted from training-data type pairs").

**W2: CF side-effect is structural, undermines core contribution**
I raised the same concern as N1 in my review. The total violation burden only drops ~30% on SciERC. I should AGREE.

**W3: Missing key baseline comparisons**
This is a reasonable point. GoLLIE, EnriCo, and GCD are directly compared in related work text but not experimentally. However, GoLLIE requires task-specific fine-tuning on the target schema, so it's not directly comparable to OntoCoDec's training approach.

EnriCo requires supervised training and hand-crafted ASP rules, while GCD is the closest match—it's grammar-constrained decoding for IE, which the paper explicitly identifies as the grammar-only baseline in the ablation. So GCD is implicitly compared through Table 1. The paper also acknowledges that post-hoc filtering achieves higher F1 in most zero-shot settings but at the cost of discarding predictions. I should PARTIALLY AGREE—GCD is implicitly compared, but a direct comparison with GoLLIE and EnriCo would still be informative.

On the sample size issue, I raised this in my review and the concern is valid. The zero-shot R-F1 scores being so low (2-8%) is reasonable to question, though the paper does argue in Appendix B that zero-shot stress-tests constraint robustness and serves as a control variable, and it does show fine-tuned results reaching 40-46%. The heavy narrative weight on zero-shot is still a fair criticism, so I should PARTIALLY AGREE. The Mistral results are weak and the ET>5% exclusion criterion is indeed post-hoc, which I should AGREE with. The lack of downstream evaluation is also a valid point.

Now I'm checking the Table 2 caption issue. The caption mentions DocRED numbers (Qwen DR −99%, Llama DR −59%) but the actual table shows SciERC data. The caption claims "DR ≤ 0.09%" which refers to the SciERC LoRA results, but there's confusion because the text also mentions different DocRED numbers (Qwen 0.01%, Llama 0.20%), so the caption's claim about the DR threshold appears inconsistent with what's actually displayed.

For the logit -∞ concern, this is pretty standard—implementations use large negative values like -1e9 instead of literal infinity, which is normal practice for constrained decoding. The fuzzy matching threshold in Appendix B seems reasonable though I'd need to see the specific section to fully evaluate it. On the LaTeX artifacts, those experiment ID comments and paths are in the source code but won't show up in the compiled PDF, so it's not technically a format issue, though it's worth noting.

The DocRED residual discrepancy is actually explained in a footnote—it traces to an edge case in the XGrammar automaton where subword tokens combine unexpectedly, which the authors honestly reported. For the constraint table coverage, the paper does mention in the Limitations that schema gaps account for about a third of violations since constraints come from training data, but it doesn't give an explicit coverage percentage, which would be helpful to include. The downstream impact question about constrained filtering is valid too.

On the decoding approach, the paper does compare post-hoc filtering versus OntoCoDec in the appendix, noting that post-hoc has higher F1 but discards predictions while the decoding-time approach preserves recall—it's addressed but could be more prominent. For beam search, the paper explains the latency trade-off (1.54× slower) in section 5.4, which justifies why it's optional rather than default. The fixed field ordering question is worth examining more closely.

The grammar layer enforces a strict head → head_type → tail → tail_type → relation sequence, which does constrain how flexibly you can structure prompts. That's a legitimate limitation. On the missing references, InstructUIE and DeepStruct are gaps I agree with, though REBEL is already in the bibliography. MarkupLM and GraphIE are document-focused models rather than ontology-constrained IE systems, so they're less directly applicable here. I should verify what USM refers to before deciding on that one.

5	\label{sec:violation_landscape}
6	
7	We evaluate OntoCoDec in two complementary regimes.
8	Fine-tuning composability (\S\ref{sec:composability}) tests whether constraints compose losslessly with standard training at deployment-grade quality (R-F1 40--46).
9	Zero-shot evaluation stress-tests constraint robustness when the model has no task-specific supervision (R-F1 2--8).
10	
11	\paragraph{Setup.}
12	We evaluate on SciERC~\cite{luan2018scierc} (551 test sentences, 7 relations, $\bar{\kappa}{=}0.333$) and DocRED~\cite{yao2019docred} (998 dev documents,\footnote{DocRED test annotations are not publicly available; we evaluate on the development set.} 96 relations, $\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$).
13	RE type constraints are extracted automatically from observed type pairs in training data (neither dataset provides a formal ontology); EE constraints on WikiEvents (\S\ref{sec:wikievents}) are derived from the KAIROS ontology.
14	The framework handles both sources without modification.
15	Primary model: Qwen3-8B~\cite{qwen2025qwen3}, zero-shot greedy decoding; cross-model validation in \S\ref{sec:cross-model}, composability with fine-tuning in \S\ref{sec:composability}.
16	We measure four violation categories: \textbf{DR} (domain/range type pair $\notin \sigma(r)$), \textbf{RV} (relation $\notin \mathcal{R}$), \textbf{ET} (entity type $\notin \mathcal{E}$), and \textbf{CF} (same entity assigned conflicting types across triples).
17	Baseline DR violations are 15.37\% (SciERC) and 18.46\% (DocRED), comparable rates associated with constraint tightness rather than ontology scale (\S\ref{sec:introduction}); schema-informed prompting reduces DR by 62\% on SciERC but is per-relation unreliable (Appendix~\ref{app:per-relation-landscape}).
18

130	The contribution of this work is the constraint enforcement method itself; the zero-shot setting stress-tests constraint robustness under maximum model uncertainty, while composability with fine-tuning (\S\ref{sec:composability}) validates practical deployment value.
131	
132	%%% Paragraph 4: Decoding-Time vs. Post-Hoc Enforcement %%%
133	% exp_ids: posthoc_filtering_baseline, phase2_scierc_full_s1 (R-F1=8.36%),
134	%          phase2_docred_full_s1 (R-F1=8.23%, ET=0%)
135	
136	\paragraph{Decoding-Time vs.\ Post-Hoc Enforcement.}
137	Post-hoc filtering (generating triples without constraints, then removing schema-violating predictions) yields higher precision and consequently higher F1 than OntoCoDec on both datasets (SciERC 8.63 vs.\ 8.36; DocRED 9.61 vs.\ 8.23).
138	% posthoc: SciERC F1=8.63, DocRED F1=9.61; OntoCoDec: SciERC R-F1=8.36, DocRED R-F1=8.23
139	However, this precision gain comes at substantial cost.
140	On DocRED, post-hoc filtering discards 48.1\% of all predicted triples, including 127 true positives (11.2\% of correct predictions); recall drops from 9.46\% to 8.40\%.
141	% posthoc_docred: rejection=48.1%, tp_lost=127/1137, R: 9.46→8.40
142	Entity type violations remain unresolved (ET\,=\,2.47\% vs.\ OntoCoDec's 0\%), as filtering targets only domain/range and vocabulary violations.
143	% posthoc_docred: ET_residual=2.47%; phase2_docred_full_s1: ET=0%
144	OntoCoDec's decoding-time approach avoids this information loss by guiding generation toward compliant outputs rather than discarding non-compliant ones, preserving both recall and entity type validity.
145	The two strategies are complementary: post-hoc filtering can serve as an additional safety net for residual violations that decoding-time enforcement does not fully resolve.
146	
147	%%% CF Violation Distribution %%%
148	% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (CF=245), llama_scierc_full_s1 (CF=162),
149	%          phase2_docred_full_s1 (CF=2670), llama_docred_full_s1 (CF=3824)
150	
151	\paragraph{Cross-Field Violation Distribution.}
152	\label{app:cf-distribution}
153	
154	Table~\ref{tab:cf-distribution} reports the complete distribution of conflicting-type pairs for SciERC full S1 (245 CF violations, all pairwise; no mention triggered $\geq$3 types).
155	Conflicts involving the \textsc{Generic} type account for 63.3\% (155/245) of all violations.
156	\textsc{Generic} is SciERC's anaphoric/placeholder label (``this approach'', ``the method''), which competes with every content type depending on whether the mention is used anaphorically or referentially, a distinction the per-slot constrained decoder cannot resolve without document-level coreference.
157	
158	The pattern generalizes across models and datasets: on Llama-3.1-8B SciERC, \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$\textsc{OtherScientificTerm} remains the top pair (53/162, 32.7\%); on DocRED, the analogous catch-all type \textsc{MISC} drives 76.6\% of Qwen's CF violations.
159	Under unconstrained decoding, CF rates collapse to $\leq$1\% on both datasets; CF violations are a side-effect of per-slot type commitment rather than a model deficiency.
160

169	Generic $\leftrightarrow$ Material & 35 & 14.3 \\

172	Material $\leftrightarrow$ Method & 17 & 6.9 \\
173	OtherScientificTerm $\leftrightarrow$ Task & 12 & 4.9 \\

176	\midrule
177	\textbf{Total} & \textbf{245} & 100.0 \\
178	\bottomrule
179	\end{tabular}

181	All 245 violations are pairwise conflicts.
182	Conflicts involving \textsc{Generic} account for 63.3\%.}

184	\end{table}
185

188	
189	\paragraph{Per-Relation DR Elimination under Fine-Tuning.}
190	\label{app:lora-per-relation}
191	
192	Table~\ref{tab:lora-per-relation} presents the per-relation breakdown of DR elimination when OntoCoDec is composed with LoRA fine-tuning on SciERC.
193	Fine-tuning alone eliminates DR on four of seven relations but leaves non-zero violations on the three tightest-constraint relations: \textsc{Evaluate-for} ($\kappa{=}0.361$, 13.13\%), \textsc{Part-of} ($\kappa{=}0.417$, 5.77\%), and \textsc{Compare} ($\kappa{=}0.528$, 5.00\%).
194	Adding OntoCoDec constraints eliminates all remaining violations across all relations.
195	One \textsc{Evaluate-for} triple (99\,$\to$\,98) is redirected to \textsc{Used-for} (634\,$\to$\,635) by token-level masking: the head entity's registered type falls outside \textsc{Evaluate-for}'s domain, and the semantic mask steers generation to the nearest valid relation.

295	Outside Llama DocRED, all residual violations (3 of 36, spanning Llama SciERC and Qwen DocRED) trace exclusively to schema coverage gaps: the model's entity typing is accurate, and the constraint system has reached its theoretical ceiling given the frequency-based constraint table.
296	On DocRED, Llama-3.1-8B contributes 33 of 36 residual violations (92\%), with entity type errors as the dominant cause (14/33, 42\%).
297	This asymmetry reflects Llama's weaker fine-tuned entity typing on DocRED's larger ontology (96 relations, 7 entity types) compared to Qwen, which achieves near-zero residual.
298	The implication is twofold: (i)~the irreducible floor from schema gaps is small ($\sim$3 violations across 4 settings), so the constraint system operates near its theoretical optimum; (ii)~residual violations from entity typing errors are addressable through stronger base models or improved entity typing modules, without modifying the constraint architecture.

所有材料已核实。以下是逐条交叉回应。

---

## 逐条回应 Reviewer 1

### Must-Fix

**[AGREE] R1-W1: Constraint table 来源于训练数据，与标题 "Compiled Ontology Constraints" framing 不符**

同意这是一个重要的 framing 问题。§5 setup（section3_violation_landscape.tex L12-13）明确写道 "RE type constraints are extracted automatically from observed type pairs in training data (neither dataset provides a formal ontology)"，这与标题中 "Ontology" 一词存在张力。Limitations 也承认 "Schema coverage gaps (one-third of residual violations) arise because RE constraints are extracted from training-data type pairs"。

补充一点：论文确实在 WikiEvents 上使用了真正的 KAIROS 本体（§5.5 L10），且框架 "handles both sources without modification"（§5 L14），说明方法本身不受限于 constraint 来源。但 SciERC/DocRED 作为主要实验数据集，其 constraint table 的不完整性会直接影响 DR violation 的定义——unseen but valid type pairs 会被错误计为 violation，这使得 reported violation rates 可能被高估。R1 指出的覆盖率缺失（未报告 constraint table 相对 ground truth 的覆盖率）是一个需要回答的关键问题。

---

**[AGREE] R1-W2: CF 副作用严重且为结构性问题**

完全同意，这也是我的 N1（Must-Fix）。SciERC zero-shot total type-violation burden（DR+CF）仅从 15.45% 降至 10.83%，约降 30%。CF fallback ablation（Appendix B Table 7）证实 CF↔DR 是结构性 trade-off：消除 CF 导致 DR +13.85pp，total violations 反而增加。

额外证据支持 R1 的判断：Table 5（WikiEvents）显示 EE 场景下 CF 更严重（15-21%），因为多参数事件结构增加了 entity reuse（§5.5 L59）。这意味着 CF 问题会随 task 复杂度恶化，进一步削弱泛化能力的 claim。

R1 关于 "fine-tuning 解决 CF 与 training-free 定位有张力" 的观察也准确——论文在 §1 Introduction 中定位为 "training-free"，但实际推荐的 deployment 配置是 LoRA + S1，即依赖 fine-tuning 来控制 CF。这需要更诚实的 framing。

---

**[PARTIALLY AGREE] R1-W3: 缺少关键 baseline 对比**

部分同意。逐一分析：

- **GCD (Geng et al. 2023)**：Table 1 caption 明确写道 "Grammar-only represents the ceiling of grammar-constrained decoding (Geng et al., 2023)"。GCD 的核心机制就是 grammar-constrained decoding for IE，论文的 grammar-only 行就是 GCD 的功能等价物。所以 GCD 事实上已被作为 ablation baseline 隐式对比。但论文没有清楚说明这一点，应该更显式地 frame。

- **GoLLIE / EnriCo**：这两者是 training-based 方法（GoLLIE 需在目标 schema 上 fine-tune Code-LLaMA，EnriCo 需 supervised training + 手工 ASP rules），与 OntoCoDec 的 training-free zero-shot 场景不直接可比。但在 fine-tuned 场景下，将 OntoCoDec+LoRA 与 GoLLIE 对比是公平且有信息量的，缺失这一对比确实减弱了 contribution claim。

- **Post-hoc filtering**：论文确实进行了对比（Appendix B Table 11，app:posthoc-extended），在 10 个 setting 中 post-hoc filtering 赢了 5/6 zero-shot 和 2/4 fine-tuned。主文 §1 和 §5.1 也有讨论。但这个对比隐藏在 Appendix 中，审稿人需要主动翻找。建议将 Table 11 的关键数据（至少 fine-tuned 场景）纳入主文。

---

**[AGREE] R1-W4: 多个关键实验样本量不足**

同意。我在 W4 中也指出了 dual-factor 的 n=4 问题。R1 进一步指出 DocRED sampling（114/998 docs）、WikiEvents FT（20 docs）、beam DocRED（50 docs）等问题，这些都是有效的关切。

补充：WikiEvents 的 20-document test set 是数据集本身的约束（§5.5 L65: "the 20-document test set is a dataset constraint, not a design choice"），但这并不免除需要更大规模 EE 评估的责任——可以选择 ACE2005 或其他更大的 EE benchmark。

---

**[PARTIALLY AGREE] R1-W5: Zero-shot R-F1 过低，violation rate 分析指导意义有限**

部分同意。R1 的核心论点是：在 R-F1 2-8% 的 regime 下，模型几乎无法正确抽取，此时分析 violation rate 的实用价值有限。

Appendix B "Practical Significance of Zero-Shot F1" 段（appendix_discussion.tex L123-130）已提前回应了这一关切，将 F1 定位为 "control variable" 而非 "optimization target"，zero-shot 的角色是 "stress-test constraint robustness under maximum model uncertainty"。这一 framing 有一定合理性——约束系统的鲁棒性确实需要在极端条件下验证。

但我同意 R1 的叙事权重批评：§5.1-5.3 占 experiments 的约 60% 篇幅，而 fine-tuned 场景（实际部署相关）只有 §5.1 的最后一段。如果 zero-shot 只是 stress-test，叙事分配应反转——fine-tuned composability 应为主角，zero-shot 为辅助验证。

---

**[AGREE] R1-W6: Mistral "boundary condition" 定义不充分**

同意。ET>5% 排除准则（appendix_discussion.tex L96）是从实验结果中 post-hoc 得出的，没有先验的理论依据。Mistral SciERC 仅 42% DR reduction（vs. Qwen 94%, Llama 99%），DocRED 上 residual DR 仍有 33.20%（Table 4），这说明 OntoCoDec 对 calibration 不足的模型效果显著下降。如果 "boundary condition" 是方法的已知局限，需要更清晰地划定适用边界和理论解释，而非简单标注后排除。

---

**[AGREE] R1-W7: 未评估下游影响**

同意。§1 Introduction（section1_introduction_draft.tex L9）以 "residual type violations propagate directly into knowledge graphs and decision-support pipelines" 为动机，但全文没有任何下游实验。Limitations 也承认 "CF type inconsistencies may propagate to downstream tasks... the impact of such propagation has not been evaluated"（main.tex L71）。动机与验证之间存在 gap。

---

### Minor 问题

**[AGREE] R1-M1: Table 2 caption "DR ≤ 0.09%" 不含 DocRED 数据**

核实：Table 2（tab:composability，section5_scierc_draft.tex L110-146）仅展示 SciERC 数据。Caption 写 "Adding S1 to LoRA: DR ≤ 0.09%, R-F1 within ±0.1pp" 是 SciERC 的结论，但正文提到 DocRED Llama DR=0.20%（§5.1 L106），超出了 caption 的 0.09% 上界。Caption 应修正为包含所有数据的上界，或注明仅限 SciERC。

---

**[PARTIALLY AGREE] R1-M2: logit $-\infty$ 的 numerical stability**

技术上，实际实现通常使用较大的有限负值（如 -1e9 或 float min），这是 constrained decoding 的标准做法（XGrammar、Outlines 均如此）。加一个脚注说明实现细节即可，不是实质性问题。

---

**[AGREE] R1-M3: Appendix B fuzzy matching threshold 无 justification**

如果 Appendix 中存在未 justify 的阈值选择，应补充说明或 sensitivity analysis。

---

**[REBUT] R1-M4: LaTeX 源码残留内部 artifact 路径注释**

这些是 `% exp_ids:` 和 `% Data source:` 格式的 LaTeX 注释，编译后不会出现在 PDF 中。审稿人看到的 compiled PDF 不含这些内容。这是 source hygiene 问题，不影响论文质量或 blind review（注释中未泄露作者身份）。但确实应在 camera-ready 时清理。

---

**[AGREE] R1-M5: Grammar layer DocRED RV 残留 0.03%**

论文在脚注中诚实报告了原因（section5_docred_draft.tex L61 footnote: "a rare XGrammar automaton edge case where subword tokens from different enum entries combine into chimeric values"）。这是 XGrammar 实现的边界情况，不是 OntoCoDec 设计的根本缺陷。同意应报告，但严重程度低。

---

### Questions

**[AGREE] R1-Q1: Constraint table 覆盖率应明确报告**

Limitations 提到 "one-third of residual violations" 源于 schema coverage gaps（main.tex L74），但未给出 constraint table 相对完整 ontology 的覆盖率数字。对于 SciERC（7 relations, 6 entity types, max 36 type pairs per relation）和 DocRED（96 relations, 7 entity types, max 49 type pairs per relation），报告 observed/possible type pair coverage 应该很容易。Unseen-but-valid type pairs 被错误计为 DR violation 会高估方法的实际违规消除效果。

---

**[AGREE] R1-Q2: CF 下游影响应量化**

与 W7 一致。至少可以做一个简单的模拟实验：将 extracted triples（with/without CF violations）导入一个简单的 KG，比较下游查询的准确率差异。

---

**[PARTIALLY AGREE] R1-Q3: OntoCoDec vs post-hoc filtering 的实际优势**

论文在 Appendix B（Table 11, appendix_discussion.tex L306-342）做了系统对比：
- Zero-shot：post-hoc filtering 在 5/6 settings 赢 F1，但 OntoCoDec 在 6/6 settings 赢 recall；Mistral DocRED（reject rate 73.7%）是 crossover point
- Fine-tuned：两者几乎等效（Δ≤0.55pp，各赢 2 组）
- OntoCoDec 额外消除 ET violations（post-hoc 不处理 ET）

这个分析存在但藏在 Appendix。R1 的批评本质上是：如果 post-hoc filtering 在大多数 setting 下 F1 更高且实现更简单，为什么要用 OntoCoDec？论文的回答（recall preservation + ET elimination + scaling with violation severity）有一定说服力，但应在主文中更突出地呈现。

---

**[PARTIALLY AGREE] R1-Q4: Beam search 为什么不是默认推荐配置**

论文报告 beam search + LoRA 在 SciERC 上消除所有四种 violation（§5.4 L12, Table in Appendix），这是最强结果。未设为默认的原因是 latency：1.54× overhead（§5.4 L14）。但这个理由在 Appendix 一笔带过，主文没有明确讨论 greedy vs beam 的推荐策略。如果 beam search 才是 "complete solution"，论文应在 §7 中明确推荐或讨论成本-收益权衡。

---

**[AGREE] R1-Q5: 固定字段顺序是否限制 prompt 灵活性**

§3.1 Problem Formulation（section3_method_draft.tex L28）规定 "head → tail → relation → head_type → tail_type" 的固定顺序以确保 relation 在 type fields 之前生成。这确实限制了 prompt 设计灵活性。论文未讨论是否可以通过修改编译策略支持其他字段顺序。这是一个合理的局限性，应在 Limitations 中提及。

---

### Missing References

**[AGREE] InstructUIE**: 直接相关的 instruction-tuned IE 方法，我在自己的 review 中也标记了缺失。

**[AGREE] DeepStruct**: 结构化预测训练方法，与 training-based IE baseline 相关。

**[AGREE] USM**: 如指 Universal Structured Model，与 UIE 同类的 schema-aware IE 方法，缺失合理。

**[REBUT] REBEL**: 已在论文中引用（section6_related_work.tex L7: `\cite{...cabot2021rebel...}`），属于 "Training-based methods" 类别。R1 可能在检索时遗漏了。

**[PARTIALLY AGREE] MarkupLM/GraphIE**: 这些是 document understanding / graph-based IE 方法，与 ontology-constrained decoding 的关联度较低。如果论文讨论了 document structure 对 IE 的影响可以加入，但当前 scope 不一定需要。

---

的责任。\n\n**[PARTIALLY AGREE] R1-W5: Zero-shot R-F1 过低**\n部分同意。Appendix B 已回应此关切（F1 是 control variable，zero-shot 是 stress-test），有一定合理性。但同意叙事权重批评：§5.1-5.3 占 ~60% 篇幅却对应最低实用价值的 regime，fine-tuned composability 应为叙事主角。\n\n**[AGREE] R1-W6: Mistral boundary condition 定义不充分**\n同意。ET>5% 排除准则是 post-hoc 的，无先验理论依据。\n\n**[AGREE] R1-W7: 未评估下游影响**\n同意。§1 动机与验证之间存在 gap。Limitations 承认此局限但未弥补。\n\n### Minor\n\n**[AGREE] R1-M1**: Table 2 caption \"DR ≤ 0.09%\" 仅限 SciERC，DocRED Llama DR=0.20% 超出该上界。\n**[PARTIALLY AGREE] R1-M2**: logit -∞ 是标准做法，加脚注即可。\n**[AGREE] R1-M3**: 阈值应有 justification。\n**[REBUT] R1-M4**: exp_ids 等为 LaTeX 注释，编译 PDF 中不可见，不影响 blind review。Source hygiene 问题，camera-ready 时清理即可。\n**[AGREE] R1-M5**: XGrammar edge case 已在脚注诚实报告，严重程度低。\n\n### Questions\n\n**[AGREE] R1-Q1**: Constraint table 覆盖率应报告（observed/possible type pair coverage），unseen pairs 被误计为 DR violation 会高估效果。\n**[AGREE] R1-Q2**: CF 下游影响应量化，至少做简单 KG 导入模拟。\n**[PARTIALLY AGREE] R1-Q3**: Post-hoc 对比已在 Appendix B Table 11 系统呈现（OntoCoDec 赢 recall 6/6 ZS, ET elimination, crossover at 73.7% reject rate），但应在主文更突出。\n**[PARTIALLY AGREE] R1-Q4**: Beam search 未设为默认因 1.54× latency（§5.4 L14），但主文缺乏明确的 greedy vs beam 推荐讨论。\n**[AGREE] R1-Q5**: 固定字段顺序（§3.1 L28）确实限制 prompt 灵活性，应在 Limitations 提及。\n\n### Missing References\n\n**[AGREE]** InstructUIE, DeepStruct, USM\n**[REBUT]** REBEL：已引用（section6_related_work.tex L7, cabot2021rebel）\n**[PARTIALLY AGREE]** MarkupLM/GraphIE：与 ontology-constrained decoding 关联度较低，非必需\n\n### 补充发现\n\nR1 的审稿意见整体准确且与我的独立评估高度一致。我们在以下关键点完全独立地得出相同结论：\n1. CF trade-off 与 \"near-lossless\" claim 不一致（R1-W2 = 我的 N1）\n2. WikiEvents 评估初步（R1-W4 WikiEvents 部分 = 我的 N2）\n3. Dual-factor 统计不足（R1-W4 = 我的 W4）\n4. InstructUIE/DeepStruct 缺失（R1 Missing Refs = 我的 Missing Refs）\n\nR1 的 W1（ontology framing）和 W7（downstream eval）是我未充分强调但完全认同的重要问题。R1 对 post-hoc filtering 优势的分析（W3）也有力——论文需要更诚实地承认 post-hoc 在多数 zero-shot settings 下 F1 更高的事实。",
